$comment: Mock rationale corpus (playbook §10: solver facts -> 60-word paragraph, list-then-write). Keys are the solver option signature the caller passes as fixture_key. Every paragraph here uses ONLY facts that the matching solver fixture supplies — that is the property the real prompt enforces and the mock must not undermine.

factsUsed: All hard rules pass for the Bengaluru pack
Master bedroom in the south-west zone
default.paragraph: This option scores 78 out of 100. Circulation is 11% of the built-up area, so very little space is lost to passages. Every hard rule in the Bengaluru pack passes. The master bedroom sits in the south-west zone and the kitchen in the south-east, which follows the usual Vastu placement.

factsUsed: All three bedrooms have an external wall
Baths stacked over a single shaft on both floors
option-compact-north-entry.paragraph: The most compact of the three: circulation is just 9% of the built-up area and it scores 82. The entrance is on the north edge. All three bedrooms reach an external wall, so each gets daylight and a window. Both floors' bathrooms stack over one shaft, which keeps the plumbing simple.

factsUsed: Living and dining open to the front setback

option-wide-frontage.paragraph: This one trades compactness for frontage, scoring 71. Circulation is 14%. The living and dining open onto the front setback, giving the ground floor a wide outlook. Ground coverage is 48% against the 50% allowed, leaving a little headroom. Two car spaces fit in the stilt.

factsUsed: Pooja room in the north-east zone
No toilet in the north-east zone
option-vastu-strict.paragraph: Chosen for Vastu: it scores 94 there and 69 overall. The pooja room sits in the north-east zone and no toilet falls in the north-east at all. Circulation is 13% of the built-up area, slightly more than the other options, which is the cost of holding those placements.
